title: kbmon panels cannot say absent or timeout for themselves: mon_coord wraps mon_base's private worker, and the view calls every absent panel a missing mon_ module
goal: mon_base gives a panel's collect a way to end in absent or timeout with a reason (an exception beside Unsupported that the worker maps to its state), mon_view prints that reason in place of 'no mon_<name>.py' for an absent panel, mon_coord uses it and no longer replaces mon_base._worker, and the monitoring doc names the way

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import mon_base,mon_coord;sys.exit(1 if mon_base._worker.__module__=='mon_coord' else 0)

clauses.clause: mon_base gives a panel's collect a way to end in absent or timeout with a reason (an exception beside Unsupported that the worker maps to its state), mon_view prints that reason in place of 'no mon_<name>.py' for an absent panel, mon_coord uses it and no longer replaces mon_base._worker
the monitoring doc names the way

gates.question: How does a panel's collect end in timeout with a reason, and how does the view show the reason?

notes: Operator request 2026-10-19: make kbmon readable and useful for a human operator (summaries of what sessions do); the orchestrator's notes from watching the night run of 2026-10-19 with kbmon. Premise on origin/main 9cee34c, 2026-10-19: repro fails (mon_base._worker is mon_coord's). 2026-10-20, ST-7jjj3b4s: mon_base now has Absent, an exception a panel's collect raises; _worker turns it into state absent with {reason} as data (the bench panel uses it, so it works under --panel bench alone, where mon_coord is never imported and its patched worker is not in place). mon_coord's declare for absent could use it; the timeout half of this bug and the view's reason text (BG-rpp4dsrn) remain.
